name: Absorb LMS

verdict.line: Absorb sells the container, not the contents — it competes for the LMS line item, and every multifamily course inside it still has to be bought, built and re-written by someone on the customer's payroll.
verdict.doInstead: Do not argue platform features. Ask who writes the fair housing course, who updates it when a state changes its rules, and what that headcount costs; then price PerformanceHQ against the platform fee plus that internal content burden. If they are already locked into Absorb, position Grace Hill content delivered into it rather than a rip-and-replace.

ownership.value: Majority-owned by Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe (WCAS Fund XIII); acquired from Silversmith Capital Partners in 2021

pricing.value: Not published on the vendor site; quote-only.

positioning.value: "The AI-powered LMS that actually knows your business" / "The Industry's #1 Learning Management System" — a horizontal enterprise LMS marketed on platform capability rather than any industry vertical.

strengths.text: WCAS reports Absorb serves approximately 28 million users across 1,700 clients in 34 countries.
Publishes 20,000+ pre-built courses through its Absorb Amplify content portfolio and pre-built connectors to ADP, Workday, Salesforce and 40+ other systems.
Absorb Create offers AI-assisted course generation with quizzes, video, translations and voice-over.

gaps.text: Absorb's public site names Sony, Gap, Johnson & Johnson, Samsung and Toyota and cites healthcare, financial services and manufacturing — it publishes no multifamily or property-management vertical.
Absorb's content story is a general business catalog (Amplify) plus customer-authored courses; no fair housing, state-specific landlord-tenant or CAM/CAPS/CALP credential content is published.

whyWeWin: Grace Hill maintains the multifamily course library itself — the customer does not staff a content team to keep fair housing current.
Fair housing and state-specific compliance content ships with the product, not as a project.
Role- and property-based assignment maps to how a portfolio is actually organized, not just to HR job codes.

objections.response: Then the platform question is settled. The open question is what goes in it for site teams — ask what happens when a fair housing rule changes and who is on the hook to update the course.

doNotSay: Do not say Absorb has no compliance content — it publishes a general business and compliance catalog; the verifiable point is that it publishes no multifamily-specific library.

whenItComesUp.why: User-generated microlearning video. It's bought for culture and peer knowledge sharing, not to satisfy a compliance requirement.
whenItComesUp.say: Learnie's a peer-to-peer video thing — teams recording tips for each other. Honestly it's a decent culture tool. It just isn't what you'd point a regulator at.
whenItComesUp.avoid: Don't position it as a failed LMS. It isn't trying to be one.
whenItComesUp.redirect: Is this about people sharing what works, or about proving what they were required to know?

spiced.listenFor: They name Learnie Community Microlearning, MyLearnie, or describe microlearning app built on user-generated video already in place.
spiced.ask: Would you hand a peer-recorded video to a regulator as evidence of fair housing training?

spiced.listenFor: Learnie's content model is knowledge captured from the customer's own team plus AI generation from customer material; no vendor-authored regulated content library is published.
spiced.ask: Who reviews team-generated content before it is published to everyone?

spiced.listenFor: Whether the gap costs them money, time or exposure — or is just an annoyance.
spiced.ask: If that stayed exactly as it is for another year, what does it cost you?

spiced.listenFor: A renewal date on the Learnie contract, an audit, an acquisition, or new leadership asking what the data shows.
spiced.ask: When does the Learnie agreement come up, and what has to be decided before then?

spiced.listenFor: Whether Learnie sits on someone else's budget line — that changes who has to agree.
spiced.ask: Who else has to be comfortable with this, and what do they need to see?
